MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  MAY 19, 2025

1.  CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. in the City Hall
  Council Chamber.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Brown Schachter, Hall, Halvorsen, Munday,
  Nash, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Combs, Martin, Persichina

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Gamboa, LACSD

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Reggie Greene, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Andrea Gamble, Office Assistant

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER announced that Director Wahba will be retiring on June 9. Director
Wahba provided some parting words.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  FEBRUARY19, 2025.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY
to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 19, 2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

A.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND SILVER SADDLE LANE PEDESTRIAN
  CROSSING

Director Wahba provided an overview of the intersection at Palos Verdes Drive North and Silver
Saddle Lane/Moccasin Lane. He mentioned the various improvements made over the years,
including the ladder crosswalk, flashing beacons, yellow signs indicating pedestrians crossing,
in-pavement flashers activated by push buttons, and the presence of a crossing guard and
traffic control officer during school hours.
Director Wahba explained that the current request was to consider installing a pedestrian hybrid
beacon (HAWK) system, which would include a large overhead light that would turn red to stop
traffic. He noted that while this could be beneficial, it may not be the best application for this
particular intersection.
Reggie Greene, the Traffic Engineering Deputy, provided a detailed explanation of the HAWK
system. He described it as a hybrid between a standard traffic signal and a flashing beacon.
Greene explained how the system works for both drivers and pedestrians, and mentioned that
the estimated construction cost for this location would be about $170,000.
Greene also discussed potential upgrades to the existing rectangular rapid flashing beacon
(RRFB) system, including larger signs and beacons, and the possibility of placing beacons
overhead. He noted that a study would be needed to check if the intersection meets the warrant
for a HAWK system installation.
Mike Semos, a long-time resident, addressed the committee. He expressed his concerns about
the current amber crossing lights, stating that they only mean caution, not stop. Semos
highlighted issues such as high speeds, lack of traffic enforcement, and the potential dangers

 for pedestrians. He suggested that the HAWK system would be more effective in ensuring
drivers stop.
Committee members and staff discussed various aspects of the proposal, including:
  ●  The possibility of collecting accident data from the Lomita Sheriff's Station
  ●  The need for a comprehensive study of the intersection
  ●  The potential impact on traffic flow, especially during school hours
  ●  The effectiveness of the current crossing guard and traffic control officer
  ●  The possibility of improving visibility with larger signs or overhead beacons

After extensive discussion, the committee decided to first gather accident data before considering
a full study.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALL made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to:

  DIRECT STAFF TO GATHER TRAFFIC ACCIDENT DATA AT THE INTERSECTION OF
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND SILVER SADDLE LANE.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Hall, Halvorsen, Munday, Nash, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT: Combs, Martin, Persichina
ABSTAIN:

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  1. ROLLING HILLS ROAD BIKE LANE PROJECT UPDATE

Director Wahba provided an update on the Rolling Hills Road Bike Lane Project. He reported that
all engineering has been completed for the project. The City received a Highway Safety
Improvement (HSIP) grant from CalTrans for $250K, which has not been used. The grant money
from Metro Measure M was used to complete the engineering, design, and California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) work. The engineer’s estimate for building the project is
approximately $4.6M. The South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) has
recommended approval of the project for construction funding to Metro, and Metro’s board will
hear the request on September 25th; assuming that it is approved, the City will move forward and
release the CEQA document. The City Manager has suggested holding a workshop to engage
and inform surrounding neighbors about this project.

Director Wahba then walked the committee through the project details. He stated that Rolling
Hills Road will not be widened; however, bike lanes will be added on either side of Rolling Hills
Road. Additionally, concrete rolled curb and gutters will be installed; improvements to drainage
and storm drain inlets; creation of a pedestrian walkway from Palos Verdes Drive North to the
Torrance city limit; and some tree removal and construction of retaining walls.

The committee received and filed the update.

  2. PROPOSED ROADWAY SIGNS FOR LARIAT LANE EAST AND WEST ON
  ROLLING HILLS ROAD

Director Wahba presented the proposal for new roadway signs for Lariat Lane East and West on
Rolling Hills Road. He explained that the request came from resident Susan Gomez, who was
concerned about confusion caused by the two different Lariat Lanes.

Director Wahba stated that the proposed signs would be 4-foot by 7-foot signs, freestanding on
4-inch by 4-inch wide posts, with white reflective backgrounds and green lettering. Options were
presented for potential locations, considering visibility and potential conflicts with existing
structures or trails.

Committee members discussed various locations and aspects of the proposal, including:

  ●  The potential impact on the bridle trail
  ●  The visibility of the signs from different approaches
  ●  The possibility of including arrows on the signs
  ●  The need to consult with residents on both Lariat Lanes

After discussion, the committee decided to move forward with the proposal.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Hall, Halvorsen, Munday, Nash, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT: Combs, Martin, Persichina
ABSTAIN:

  3. SPEED LIMIT DISCUSSION ON PVDN (ASSEMBLY BILL 43)

Director Wahba introduced the discussion on potentially reducing speed limits on Palos Verdes
Drive North (PVDN) in light of Assembly Bill 43, which provides cities more flexibility in
establishing speed limits.

Reggie Greene, the Traffic Engineering Deputy, explained that the City could reduce the speed
limit. The engineering and traffic survey is the document used to determine speed limits and
amendments will be made to the document to establish the new speed limit.

Director Naughton asked about adjustments needed to signal timing. Traffic Engineering Deputy
Greene stated that he will provide an answer for this question.

Will Nicklas, a resident and Planning Commissioner, spoke in support of reducing speed limits
and provided background on his previous request to the City Council on this subject. He stated
that his request also included reducing the speed limit from 45 to 40 mph between the Lomita city
boundary and Palos Verdes Drive East since people are driving in from high-speed roads. He
also suggested requesting more patrol and enforcement on Palos Verdes Drive North; installing
speed feedback signs; and making the pass-through lane at Dapplegray school a right-turn only
lane.

In response to a question by CHAIR SCHACHTER, Deputy Gamboa stated that the change in
speed limits would not cause a concern for enforcement; however, it will take time for the public
to get used to the transition in speed changes.

Committee members and staff discussed various aspects of the proposal, including:

  ●  The potential impact on traffic flow
  ●  The need for additional signage to notify drivers of the changes
  ●  The possibility of installing speed feedback signs at key locations
  ●  The need for enforcement of the new speed limits

After extensive discussion, the committee decided to recommend the speed limit reductions to
the City Council.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER HALL to,

  RECOMMEND TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE THE REDUCTION OF THE
  SPEED LIMIT FROM THE ENTRANCE OF THE CITY ON THE EAST SIDE TO PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE NORTH DOWN TO 40 MILES PER HOUR; AND FROM PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST THROUGH HAWTHORNE BOULEVARD DROP THE SPEED
  LIMIT TO 35 MILES PER HOUR.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Hall, Halvorsen, Munday, Nash, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT: Combs, Martin, Persichina
ABSTAIN:

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
TERTZAKIAN to,

  TABLE THE SIGN DISCUSSION UNTIL THE NEXT COMMITTEE MEETING AND
  DIRECT CITY STAFF TO POTENTIALLY DO SOME RESEARCH ON AREAS WHERE
  THE SIGNS MIGHT BE MOST VIABLE FOR REVIEW.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Hall, Halvorsen, Munday, Nash, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

DIRECTOR WAHBA MENTIONED HIS UPCOMING RETIREMENT AND THANKED THE
COMMITTEE FOR THEIR SERVICE.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALL requested adding a roadkill removal agenda item to the next
meeting. He expressed concerns about the length of time it takes to remove roadkill from major
roads in the community. CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER suggested contacting the City’s
maintenance department who will pick up roadkill from streets and then they will contact animal
control to pick-up.

Director Naughton informed the committee about an upcoming mobile app that will allow residents
to report issues such as roadkill, potholes, and other concerns directly to the appropriate
department.

Mr. Semos announced that Deputy Gamboa was honored as the responder of the year at the
Rotary Responder Roundup. COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE also shared a special moment when
his son met Deputy Gamboa.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 7:48 p.m.
